facts.label: Key credit drivers
facts.text: Leverage rose between FY2025 and September 2026 because carrying debt increased faster than cash and reported LTM EBITDA. The primary cause disclosed is acquisition financing: 9M 2026 included USD 225.4 million of acquisition cash outflow, USD 424.5 million of Term Loan B proceeds and USD 277.3 million of Term Loan A repayments. A stronger counterpoint is that 9M 2026 operating cash flow exceeded the prior-year period and free cash flow was positive; it would carry more weight if the acquired businesses sustain cash generation and management directs it to debt reduction rather than further acquisitions or distributions. Basis: calculation C5; calculation C7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 20–21; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 83

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest counterweight is that FY2025 sales were distributed across two substantial product segments and the year-end order book was expected to convert predominantly in the following fiscal year; the latest release also showed a larger total backlog, including acquired Antares orders. SAT reported stronger year-over-year quarterly profit, and management said it delivered synergy commitments and remained on track for its year-end deleveraging objective. These points support demand visibility and potential acquisition benefits, but management’s statements do not establish realized cash savings or acquisition returns. The view would improve with sustained organic growth, stable segment margins after the reorganization, reported Antares cash generation and debt paydown, and disclosure of the shareholder and legal-control structure; it would weaken if acquired-business losses persist, backlog conversion slips, or further borrowing funds acquisitions or distributions without commensurate cash generation. Segment and customer disclosure; Historical recast under the new DTT structure, remaining customer distribution and recurring-revenue share; Trend comparability and revenue visibility remain incomplete; Revenue mix and operating model

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Crane NXT combines authentication, payment-verification, product-security and traceability activities, with cash generation that has covered capital spending and cash interest in the latest reported period. The creditor case is constrained by a sharp increase in carrying debt following acquisitions, carrying-value leverage above the issuer-adjusted presentation, SAT customer concentration and the acquired Antares business’s operating loss. A larger backlog and positive free cash flow provide support, but backlog is not cash and the segment reorganization limits annual comparability. The primary downside path is delayed integration or customer/order weakness reducing margins and cash conversion, slowing debt reduction and increasing dependence on future refinancing. Stated loan maturities are several years away, although principal allocations by maturity are incomplete. facts.label: Operating model and business risk synthesis
facts.text: The source evidence supports a limited competitive assessment: proprietary authentication solutions and customer use in banknotes, consumer goods and government tax stamps create differentiated product applications, while the significant SAT customer and lower DTT organic sales demonstrate concentrated demand and exposure to order timing. The documents do not quantify market share, switching costs, supplier dependence or competitor pricing, so those factors do not support a stronger competitive-position conclusion. The annual report identifies macroeconomic, trade-policy, inflation, foreign-exchange and geopolitical risks that could weaken customer demand, raise sourcing costs or make refinancing less favorable. It also reports FY2025 interest-rate and currency sensitivities, but neither those disclosures nor the subsequent interim filing quantify current demand, input-cost or refinancing sensitivities. In credit-translated SWOT terms, backlog and SAT profitability are supports; acquired-business losses, customer concentration, rising debt and non-comparable segment history are constraints; Antares’s life-science and food traceability applications are a potential growth avenue, while delayed integration or order conversion is the principal threat. facts.label: Cost structure, cash conversion and financing
facts.text: The Credit Agreement facilities have stated maturities several years beyond the latest reporting date. The latest filing does not allocate all current loan principal by maturity year, so the stated dates identify refinancing windows but not a complete maturity wall. A revolving commitment is disclosed, but current letter-of-credit use is not reported; the FY2025 filing reported USD 97.5 million of standby letters, so current undrawn liquidity cannot be inferred from that older balance. This leaves the near-term liquidity conclusion supported by positive cash and operating cash flow, while exact committed availability and facility headroom remain unestablished. facts.label: Outlook and downside
facts.text: Over the next year, the main upside is conversion of the reported backlog and realization of management’s stated FY2026 sales-growth and adjusted-margin outlook. Over a longer horizon, Antares may expand traceability exposure in life sciences and food and beverage, but the filings do not establish standalone acquired-business returns. The principal downside is a delayed integration or weaker customer and order demand: DTT’s acquired contribution would fail to cover its lower organic sales, group operating profit would weaken, and working-capital absorption could reduce free cash flow. Lower cash generation would slow debt reduction and increase reliance on refinancing, although stated facility maturities are not immediate. Cost alignment and cash retention are management levers, but the supplied evidence does not quantify savings, fixed-cost flexibility or downside runway. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Crane NXT’s disclosed product applications, backlog and positive free cash flow support debt service, while acquisition-funded leverage, Antares losses and customer concentration constrain the credit profile. ## Findings
### Bottom line

Crane NXT’s reported cash flow supports ongoing debt service, but acquisition funding pushed carrying-value net debt higher and leaves reported LTM leverage at 3.03x. Creditors should distinguish issuer-adjusted leverage from carrying-value leverage and treat the current maturity ladder as incomplete.
Basis: calculation C5; calculation C6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 3–5; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq3-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 7–9

The cash flow statement records USD 184.5 million of operating cash flow and USD 139.5 million of free cash flow for 9M 2026, while acquisition and financing activity left carrying-value net debt at USD 1,131.4 million at September 30, 2026. Management reports 2.5x net leverage using net debt before deferred financing costs and TTM Adjusted EBITDA; the comparable ratio using balance-sheet carrying debt and reported LTM EBITDA is 3.03x. Missing instrument-level principal schedules limit exact maturity-wall and secured-debt calculations.
Basis: calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 3–5, 20–21; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq3-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 7–9
### Key credit drivers

Leverage rose between FY2025 and September 2026 because carrying debt increased faster than cash and reported LTM EBITDA. The primary cause disclosed is acquisition financing: 9M 2026 included USD 225.4 million of acquisition cash outflow, USD 424.5 million of Term Loan B proceeds and USD 277.3 million of Term Loan A repayments. A stronger counterpoint is that 9M 2026 operating cash flow exceeded the prior-year period and free cash flow was positive; it would carry more weight if the acquired businesses sustain cash generation and management directs it to debt reduction rather than further acquisitions or distributions.
Basis: calculation C5; calculation C7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 20–21; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 83

Reported interest coverage remains positive, but FFO-to-debt is not calculable because the issuer does not report FFO or enough components to define it consistently. The adjusted measures exclude special items and include Antares Vision for periods before acquisition; they are useful as management’s supplemental view, not a substitute for GAAP cash flow or carrying-value debt.
Basis: calculation C6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 4–5; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq3-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 7–10

### Post-period events and cash-flow quality

The company completed the Antares Vision acquisition on March 31, 2026 and funded it in part with the new Term Loan B. The acquisition added revenue and a new business to DTT, but its separate contribution to post-close reported cash flow and EBITDA is not isolated in these statements. At September 30, carrying debt was USD 1,382.5 million, while unrestricted cash was USD 251.1 million; restricted cash of USD 10.1 million remains outside net debt. The reported cash flow statement’s USD 261.2 million closing balance includes that restricted cash.
Basis: calculation C5; calculation C11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 3–5, 9, 20–21

Operating cash flow increased from USD 135.7 million in 9M 2025 to USD 184.5 million in 9M 2026 as the reported working-capital cash use narrowed from USD 41.9 million to USD 16.4 million. The same period included USD 45.0 million of capital spending and USD 225.4 million of acquisition payments, leaving USD 139.5 million of free cash flow before acquisition spending. Positive free cash flow supports debt service, but acquisition cash outflow and recurring dividends constrain the amount available for deleveraging.
Basis: calculation C7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 4

Contract liabilities are advance payments from customers and increased from USD 87.3 million at FY2025 to USD 158.4 million at September 2026. This liability funds operations before the related performance obligation is fulfilled; delivery, cancellation or other settlement requirements can reverse that float into working-capital cash use. The filings do not quantify refunds or customer-specific delivery timing, so the size and timing of any reversal are not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 91, 103; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 17

Reported LTM EBITDA divided by cash interest paid is 5.62x at September 2026 versus 6.35x for FY2025. This is a cash-paid coverage measure; P&L interest expense was USD 58.7 million for 9M 2026 and cannot be substituted for the USD 51.4 million of cash interest paid in that period. FFO is not reported, so FFO-to-debt and a separate FFO-interest trajectory are not calculable.
Basis: calculation C4; calculation C6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 54

The quarter-end release states that its USD 460.3 million TTM Adjusted EBITDA includes Antares Vision for periods before acquisition and that its USD 1,161.5 million net debt is calculated before deferred financing costs. Those definitions produce management’s 2.5x rounded ratio. Using the balance-sheet debt carrying value and the reported LTM EBITDA gives 3.03x; the two ratios differ in both numerator basis and EBITDA definition. Carrying value is retained for the credit metric; the issuer ratio is preserved as a supplemental management view.
Basis: calculation C5; calculation C6; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq3-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 20

The 6.55% notes are due in November 2036 and the 4.20% notes are due in March 2048. The Term Loan A and Revolving Facility are scheduled to mature December 15, 2030; Term Loan B is scheduled to mature December 15, 2032. The company reports a USD 800.0 million revolving commitment and USD 229.9 million outstanding at September 2026. It does not give current principal by loan maturity or a current letter-of-credit amount against the revolver, so the date ladder cannot quantify all principal due or net committed availability exactly. No facility expiry within twelve months is identified in the stated maturity terms.
Basis: calculation C8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 105–109

The November 4 release revised FY2026 guidance to approximately 14% sales growth, adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 24%, and adjusted EPS of USD 4.32 to USD 4.42. It also declared a fourth-quarter dividend payable December 9, 2026. The dividend was scheduled but not paid by the November 18 cutoff and therefore is not included in pro forma net debt. The updated guidance is management’s forward-looking view, not a realized financial result.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Crane NXT’s secure-payment and authentication activities have identifiable customer uses and disclosed order backlog, but a significant SAT customer, recent acquisitions and a reorganized operating structure make revenue concentration, segment comparability and acquired-business returns material creditor questions.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8, 89–91; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 13–15; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq3-htm.htm.jsonl, page 6
### Key findings

- The operating model spans payment-verification equipment and software, field services, banknotes, product security and authentication. FY2025 sales were nearly balanced between CPI and SAT, but the segment structure changed after Antares Vision was acquired and CPI was combined with Antares in DTT. Annual and current segment figures therefore do not form a like-for-like time series.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8, 89–90; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 14–15; calculation C1

- A persistent customer concentration is disclosed within SAT: one individually significant customer generated USD 210.7 million of FY2025 sales, after USD 209.2 million in FY2024 and USD 213.1 million in FY2023. The FY2025 amount equaled 26.0% of SAT and 12.7% of total company sales, exposing results to customer-specific order and renewal decisions even though the customer is not named.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 91; calculation C7

- Acquisition risk is material to current operating analysis: Antares Vision contributed sales while reporting an operating loss during 2026, and DTT’s reported quarterly operating profit and margin were below the prior-year quarter even as acquired sales lifted the segment’s total. The issuer attributes Antares’s operating loss to acquisition-related amortization and transaction costs, but standalone cash returns remain unestablished.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 13–15; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq3-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 6

- Ownership evidence establishes public listing and acquired operating assets, but does not identify current beneficial shareholders, their economic stakes or shareholder-level control rights. The public-company evidence cannot support a sponsor-alignment conclusion; the detailed ownership view remains insufficiently established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 115

- Acquisition funding and ordinary dividends are disclosed, but the pinned documents do not provide purchase multiples, transaction-level pro forma leverage or enough legal detail to assess acquisition returns and capacity. The evidence supports monitoring cash retention and integration outcomes, not a conclusion that shareholder extraction occurred.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 54, 83–84; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 8–10, 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 4
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest counterweight is that FY2025 sales were distributed across two substantial product segments and the year-end order book was expected to convert predominantly in the following fiscal year; the latest release also showed a larger total backlog, including acquired Antares orders. SAT reported stronger year-over-year quarterly profit, and management said it delivered synergy commitments and remained on track for its year-end deleveraging objective. These points support demand visibility and potential acquisition benefits, but management’s statements do not establish realized cash savings or acquisition returns. The view would improve with sustained organic growth, stable segment margins after the reorganization, reported Antares cash generation and debt paydown, and disclosure of the shareholder and legal-control structure; it would weaken if acquired-business losses persist, backlog conversion slips, or further borrowing funds acquisitions or distributions without commensurate cash generation.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 89–90; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 13–15; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq3-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 6
### Limitations

- The conclusion on shareholder influence and governance remains limited because the supplied filings do not identify current beneficial owners, ownership percentages or investor-specific voting arrangements; the current proxy and related governance documents are needed to establish whether ownership is concentrated.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 115

- The conclusion on Antares and DLR acquisition economics remains limited because transaction-level purchase multiples, acquired-business pro forma leverage and standalone cash-flow returns are not supplied; creditors cannot test whether acquisition consideration is supported by sustainable earnings and cash conversion.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 8–13

- FY2025 control conclusions do not cover DLR’s internal-control systems, which were excluded from the company’s control assessment as a recently acquired business; this reduces assurance over the acquired operation’s processes until integration is completed.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 112–113

- Annual CPI/SAT sales and the current DTT/SAT structure are not directly comparable because the current segment definition combines CPI with Antares; this limits trend conclusions for segment growth, margins and capital intensity.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 89; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15
- This analysis establishes operating and transaction facts only; by itself it cannot support a final debt-capacity, recovery or investment view, so those decisions require their own analysis.
### Company and operating model

Crane NXT sells specialized equipment, associated software and authentication products and services. FY2025 filing revenue detail shows balanced segment totals but different product composition: CPI was predominantly products with a smaller service stream, while SAT was predominantly banknotes and security products with a substantial authentication business. The filing also identifies one individually significant SAT customer; it does not identify the customer or describe contract duration.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Crane NXT acquired OpSec Security in May 2024 for a base purchase price of USD 270.0 million on a cash-free, debt-free basis; net cash paid was USD 268.4 million, funded with USD 210.0 million from the revolving facility and cash on hand. De La Rue Authentication Solutions was acquired in May 2025 at a base price of GBP 300.0 million, cash-free and debt-free; the filing reports final net cash paid of USD 391.1 million and use of Term Loan A. The sources do not provide transaction-level pro forma leverage or a purchase multiple for either acquisition.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 83–84

Crane NXT began its multi-phase Antares Vision acquisition in December 2025, paying EUR 117.3 million, approximately USD 137.8 million, for an initial 32.3% interest. The remaining shares were acquired through the tender and squeeze-out completed in March 2026 for EUR 244.2 million, approximately USD 281.9 million; the filing reports total consideration of USD 416.9 million. Antares provides inspection, detection and track-and-trace systems for life-sciences and food-and-beverage customers. Its post-acquisition contribution included operating losses attributed by the issuer to acquisition-related amortization and transaction costs, so standalone cash returns are not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 8–10, 13

The Fifth Amendment in December 2025 established a EUR 430 million senior secured delayed-draw Term Loan B due in December 2032, extended the existing Term Loan A and revolving facility maturities to December 2030, and increased the revolving commitment to USD 800.0 million. A July 2026 repricing increased the Term Loan B to EUR 480 million; the incremental EUR 50 million and cash on hand were used primarily to repay Term Loan A. The Q3 filing also reports borrowings and repayments used to fund Antares, repay assumed Antares debt and support working capital. The executed amendment texts are not included in the pinned sources, limiting conclusions about covenant capacity and collateral terms.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 21; Source readiness (CP-0)

## Findings
### Bottom line

Crane NXT’s positive cash generation and stated long-dated facility maturities support debt service, but acquisition-funded leverage and weak acquired-segment profitability leave creditors exposed to integration and refinancing execution.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21
### Key findings

Reported revenue growth overstates underlying momentum: acquisitions, including Antares Vision, supplied most of the latest reported increase while DTT organic sales declined. DTT’s Q3 margin is below the former CPI-only perimeter, but segment reorganization and acquired-intangible amortization make this comparison non-like-for-like. Integration remains a near-term cash-flow test rather than a proven source of deleveraging.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq3-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 13–15

Positive free cash flow supports debt service, but does not yet demonstrate a reduction in creditor risk: carrying-value net debt increased and reported LTM leverage is higher than at FY2025. The issuer’s lower adjusted leverage uses a different debt and EBITDA definition, so the two ratios should not be blended.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2-03; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 3–5; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq3-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10

Customer concentration is material within SAT: one unnamed customer accounted for a substantial share of sales, leaving that segment exposed to customer order, renewal and product decisions that cannot be monitored through named-customer disclosures.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 91; calculation C2-05
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest counterweight is cash generation alongside higher reported order backlog. The latest release also gives FY2026 sales-growth and adjusted EBITDA margin guidance, though this remains management’s forward-looking view rather than a realized result. Those indicators could support faster deleveraging if backlog converts, acquired businesses move toward operating profitability and cash is retained for debt reduction. The view would improve with successive periods of organic growth, DTT margin recovery and lower carrying net debt; it would weaken if acquired sales mask continued organic contraction, Antares operating losses persist or distributions and further acquisitions consume cash generation.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq3-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 13–15; calculation C2-04
### Limitations

- The downside case is qualitative because the latest release gives broad annual sales and adjusted-margin guidance but no integrated quarterly cash forecast or volume, price, working-capital and cost sensitivities; this prevents a defensible estimate of stressed debt-service capacity and liquidity runway.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 2–5; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq3-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3

- This fundamental view does not establish the relative value of any specific Crane NXT bond or loan because no instrument-level market price is assessed; it should not be used as a security selection or position-size conclusion.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)
### Credit view

Crane NXT combines authentication, payment-verification, product-security and traceability activities, with cash generation that has covered capital spending and cash interest in the latest reported period. The creditor case is constrained by a sharp increase in carrying debt following acquisitions, carrying-value leverage above the issuer-adjusted presentation, SAT customer concentration and the acquired Antares business’s operating loss. A larger backlog and positive free cash flow provide support, but backlog is not cash and the segment reorganization limits annual comparability. The primary downside path is delayed integration or customer/order weakness reducing margins and cash conversion, slowing debt reduction and increasing dependence on future refinancing. Stated loan maturities are several years away, although principal allocations by maturity are incomplete.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 13–15, 20–21; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq3-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 6, 9

### Operating model and business risk synthesis

Crane NXT sells equipment, software and services used to verify currency and payments, protect physical products, and authenticate or trace products through supply chains. SAT’s banknote and product-security activity provides a current profit offset to DTT; DTT combines the former CPI business with Antares Vision. This addition broadens the product and end-market set but creates integration risk and makes pre- and post-acquisition segment comparisons non-like-for-like. The filings identify a persistent individually significant SAT customer, but do not name it or disclose its contract duration. Those facts constrain conclusions about customer switching costs and renewal resilience.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8, 89–91; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 14–15

The source evidence supports a limited competitive assessment: proprietary authentication solutions and customer use in banknotes, consumer goods and government tax stamps create differentiated product applications, while the significant SAT customer and lower DTT organic sales demonstrate concentrated demand and exposure to order timing. The documents do not quantify market share, switching costs, supplier dependence or competitor pricing, so those factors do not support a stronger competitive-position conclusion. The annual report identifies macroeconomic, trade-policy, inflation, foreign-exchange and geopolitical risks that could weaken customer demand, raise sourcing costs or make refinancing less favorable. It also reports FY2025 interest-rate and currency sensitivities, but neither those disclosures nor the subsequent interim filing quantify current demand, input-cost or refinancing sensitivities. In credit-translated SWOT terms, backlog and SAT profitability are supports; acquired-business losses, customer concentration, rising debt and non-comparable segment history are constraints; Antares’s life-science and food traceability applications are a potential growth avenue, while delayed integration or order conversion is the principal threat.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 13, 47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 13–15, 34; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq3-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 6
### Cost structure, cash conversion and financing

Operating cash flow of USD 184.5 million and free cash flow of USD 139.5 million in 9M 2026 exceed the prior-year period. The improvement supports debt service, but cash flow was not fully available for principal reduction: acquisition payments and dividends competed with deleveraging, and the Antares contribution has not been separately reconciled to post-close EBITDA and cash generation. Reported LTM cash-interest cover remains positive, but carrying-value net debt and leverage increased since year-end. The company’s 2.5x figure uses adjusted EBITDA and principal before financing costs; it is not directly comparable with the 3.03x carrying-value net leverage calculation.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 3–5, 20–21; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq3-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; calculation C2-03; calculation C2-04

The Credit Agreement facilities have stated maturities several years beyond the latest reporting date. The latest filing does not allocate all current loan principal by maturity year, so the stated dates identify refinancing windows but not a complete maturity wall. A revolving commitment is disclosed, but current letter-of-credit use is not reported; the FY2025 filing reported USD 97.5 million of standby letters, so current undrawn liquidity cannot be inferred from that older balance. This leaves the near-term liquidity conclusion supported by positive cash and operating cash flow, while exact committed availability and facility headroom remain unestablished.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 105–109
### Outlook and downside

Over the next year, the main upside is conversion of the reported backlog and realization of management’s stated FY2026 sales-growth and adjusted-margin outlook. Over a longer horizon, Antares may expand traceability exposure in life sciences and food and beverage, but the filings do not establish standalone acquired-business returns. The principal downside is a delayed integration or weaker customer and order demand: DTT’s acquired contribution would fail to cover its lower organic sales, group operating profit would weaken, and working-capital absorption could reduce free cash flow. Lower cash generation would slow debt reduction and increase reliance on refinancing, although stated facility maturities are not immediate. Cost alignment and cash retention are management levers, but the supplied evidence does not quantify savings, fixed-cost flexibility or downside runway.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 13–15, 21–22; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq3-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 6

### Strengths and weaknesses

The principal strengths are demonstrated post-capex cash generation, a larger backlog, SAT’s current profit contribution and debt facilities with stated maturities several years beyond the latest reporting date. Each provides time or cash-flow capacity to service debt if backlog converts and acquired activities improve.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX99.1_2026-09-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq3-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21

The principal weaknesses are the increase in carrying-value net debt, the acquisition-related operating loss and lower DTT margin, persistent SAT customer concentration, and incomplete loan maturity allocation. Together they reduce visibility into the pace of deleveraging, concentration resilience and the amount of debt requiring refinancing at each stated date.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 91; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 13–15, 20–21
### Overall credit view

Crane NXT’s disclosed product applications, backlog and positive free cash flow support debt service, while acquisition-funded leverage, Antares losses and customer concentration constrain the credit profile. The business cannot be ranked against typical leveraged-credit issuers from these issuer-only materials. Financial capacity weakened on a carrying-value basis since FY2025, although positive cash flow moderates the pressure. Refinancing depends on organic demand, acquired-margin repair, cash retention and execution ahead of stated facility dates; the principal downside is weaker orders or delayed integration reducing margins and cash conversion. A more definitive view needs a current loan-principal schedule by maturity and an integrated cash forecast that tests customer, margin and working-capital shocks.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 13–15, 20–21; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq3-htm.jsonl, page 6
